gbm_population_evidence.quote: Part I:1) Histologically confirmed high-grade glioma (WHO classification grade III or IV)

Part II: Patients with histological or cytological diagnosis of glioblastoma according to World Health Organization (WHO) classification (2021) who received surgical treatment for the first time and standard concurrent chemoradiotherapy

candidate_evidence.quote: HX301 is an investigational drug that has not yet been approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) or any other regulatory authorities for commercial purposes.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: Patients with recurrent or progressive clinically assessed disease according to RANO criteria with evaluable lesions
who received surgical treatment for the first time and standard concurrent chemoradiotherapy and who have not received any other prior treatment

role_evidence.quote: A Phase IIa Clinical Study of HX301 Alone or in Combination with Temozolomide in Patients with High-Grade Glioma (Grade III and IV)

agents.drug_class_hint: investigational oral small-molecule kinase inhibitor (development code HX301)
arms: Patients received HX301/+Temozolomide treatment at assigned dose level on a 4 weeks basis

role_evidence.quote: Part II: Combination therapy phase: HX301 will be administered in combination with temozolomide approximately 4-6 weeks after completion of chemoradiotherapy.

agents.drug_class_hint: alkylating agent, GBM standard of care (adjuvant Stupp backbone)
arms: Patients received HX301/+Temozolomide treatment at assigned dose level on a 4 weeks basis

coder_notes: Single registered arm with two parts: Part I HX301 monotherapy in recurrent grade III/IV high-grade glioma; Part II HX301 + adjuvant temozolomide (standard 150-200 mg/m2 D1-5) after Stupp chemoradiotherapy in newly diagnosed glioblastoma (WHO 2021), followed by HX301 maintenance. Regimen coded combination because the experimental arm includes temozolomide in Part II; Part I alone would be monotherapy. Temozolomide is the standard adjuvant backbone (soc_backbone). Arm label copied without the trailing colon. No mechanism stated in the record.
